references.supports: Debiased NEO orbital and absolute-magnitude distributions and source-region priors.
references.does_not_support: The selector's exact component weights, sky-density exponentials, or class completeness constants.

references.supports: ZTF twilight searches for interior-Earth objects at solar elongations down to about 35 degrees.
references.does_not_support: The selector's exact preference peak, eligibility bounds, scarcity curve, or component weights.

references.supports: Population-completeness estimation using discovery and re-detection statistics.
references.does_not_support: The selector's exact per-class completeness constants or component weights.

empirical_evidence.supports: Separating broad eligibility from narrow preference: v1 admitted 0/1 ZTF Aten and 1/7 ZTF Atira positives while admitting every searched null.
empirical_evidence.does_not_support: Coefficient fitting, calibrated discovery probability, or causal yield claims.

empirical_evidence.supports: Revising the aten/ieo preference peaks: all 56 real Aten I41-attributed discoveries fall at elongation 99.4-173.7 deg (none inside the prior 60-100 deg window) and all 7 real Atira I41-attributed discoveries fall at elongation 39.5-53.1 deg (none inside the prior 20-45 deg window). A real per-mode coefficient-fit attempt (Skills/fit_field_ranking_coefficients.py) independently found geometry_score stably anti-correlated with discovery outcome in both modes (bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero), consistent with this raw pattern.
empirical_evidence.does_not_support: Fitted coefficients for survey_scarcity_score or population_score, whose bootstrap CIs did not exclude zero in at least one mode; a calibrated discovery probability; or a claim that the new peaks are optimal rather than a directionally-corrected, still-uncalibrated prior.

limitations: Exact coefficients remain explicit operator priors, not fitted literature coefficients.
Eligibility bounds are evidence-audited search bounds; preference peaks remain uncalibrated priorities.
The policy is deterministic and explainable but is not a calibrated probability model.

The v3 aten/ieo preference-peak revision is supported by real but still small samples (56/21 aten, 7/7 ieo source-aligned records); it corrects a clear directional error, not a precisely fitted optimum.
